title: `ExactCFbend` ignores the skew dipole `k_skew[0]`
summary: `ExactCFbend` leaves the skew-dipole coefficient `k_skew[0]` out of its orbital kick, so a skew dipole produces no vertical steering. In the element's curvilinear field model the skew dipole gives Bₓ/(Bρ) = kₛ/(1 + hx), with Bρ the magnetic rigidity, h the curvature and kₛ = `k_skew[0]`, so an on-axis particle must leave a body of length L with `py` = kₛ·L. For an on-axis proton in `ExactCFbend(ds=0.7, k_normal=[0.3], k_skew=[0.02])`, `py` is 0 instead of 0.01400, with one and with four slices.

title: `RFCavity` spin transport rotates spin without a field and uses `sqrt(1+pt²)` for βγ
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), `RFCavity` rotates the spin incorrectly: one spin-coupling term omits the on-axis field profile, and two divide by √(1 + γ²) instead of the reference momentum βγ. Thomas–BMT spin precession vanishes where the field is zero and starts at the entrance with rate |dSₓ/ds| = E·`px`·(G + 1/(γ + 1)) for on-axis field E and magnetic anomaly G. For a proton at γ = 2, a cavity with `cos_coefficients=[0]` (no field) turns the spin from (0, 0, 1) to (−0.002864, −0.001091, 1.000); with E = 0.2 m⁻¹ and `px` = 0.001, the entrance rate is 3.294e-4 m⁻¹ instead of 4.252e-4 m⁻¹. Settings describing the same field give the same orbit but different spins; the orbit is unaffected.

title: `DipEdge(modify_ref_part=True)` deflects the reference by the beam-normalized kick
summary: With the nonlinear `DipEdge` model and `modify_ref_part=True`, ImpactX adds the fringe kick, normalized to the reference momentum P₀, directly to the reference particle's `px`, which is stored in units of mc. Since P₀/(mc) = βγ, the reference must instead be deflected by βγ times the kick the beam receives with `modify_ref_part=False`. For `psi` = 0.25 rad, `rc` = 1 m, `g` = 0.1 m and a reference entering along the axis, the reference `px` is −0.004474 at every energy instead of −0.007749 at γ = 2 and −0.04452 at γ = 10. The reference deflection is too small above βγ = 1 and too large below; the kick applied to the beam with `modify_ref_part=False` is not affected.

title: Soft-edge elements and their `reverse()` do not cancel in a lattice
summary: A `SoftQuadrupole`, `SoftSolenoid` or `RFCavity` followed by its `reverse()` copy in a lattice does not return particles to their initial coordinates, although the manual documents `reverse()` as undoing the original element. Lattice tracking resets the field-profile origin at each element, so the reversed element (negative `ds`) integrates outside its field profile; with a flat profile it reduces to a drift of length −`ds`. Pushing the reversed element directly, which keeps the forward element's profile origin, closes the round trip to 2.1e-16. With a constant profile (`cos_coefficients=[2]`, `ds` = 0.7 m), the largest coordinate error after the pair, in metres or normalized momentum, is 0.01080 for `SoftQuadrupole`, 0.004498 for `SoftSolenoid` and 0.002723 for `RFCavity`.

title: Periodic `PolygonAperture` mirrors asymmetric polygons
summary: A `PolygonAperture` with a nonzero period `repeat_x` (or `repeat_y`) folds coordinates into the central cell through their absolute value, which mirrors every negative coordinate. For a polygon that is not symmetric about x = 0 (or y = 0), particles inside the aperture are removed and particles whose mirror image lies inside it pass, whereas repeating the aperture with a period must leave a point already in the central period unchanged. For a rectangle with x ∈ [−0.3, 0.1] m and y ∈ [−0.2, 0.2] m and `repeat_x=1`, a particle at x = −0.2 m, inside the rectangle, is removed; with `repeat_x=0` it survives. Polygons symmetric about the folded axis are unaffected.

title: Linear `CFbend` returns NaN at a zero focusing frequency
summary: The linear `CFbend` returns NaN coordinates when a focusing frequency is zero: gradient `k` = 0 gives NaN `y` and `py`, and `k` = −1/`rc`² (bend radius `rc`), which cancels horizontal focusing, gives NaN `x`, `px` and `t`. The transfer functions have finite limits there, matched by `Sbend` at `k` = 0 and by a gradient raised by 1e-9 m⁻². When rounding leaves a residue of −1.4e-17 m⁻² in the horizontal focusing `k` + 1/`rc`², the result is finite but wrong: for `rc` = 1/0.3 m, `k` = −0.09 m⁻² and `ds` = 0.7 m, `x` is 0.02770 m instead of 0.03025 m and `t` is 0.01115 m instead of 0.01314 m.

title: `ExactCFbend` with `k_normal[0]=0` returns NaN
summary: An `ExactCFbend` with zero dipole strength, `k_normal[0]=0`, and any coefficient slot above the dipole, even one set to zero, returns NaN in `x`, `px`, `y`, `py` and `t`, because its multipole kick divides by a bend radius stored as zero. At zero curvature the element must reduce to the corresponding straight multipole; for a quadrupole that is `ExactQuad`, which agrees with an independent integration of the square-root (exact) Hamiltonian. For a proton with all six coordinates nonzero, `ExactCFbend(ds=0.7, k_normal=[0, 0.8])` gives NaN, while `ExactQuad(ds=0.7, k=0.8)` with the same integrator gives `x` = 0.02394 m, `px` = 0.01032 and `y` = −0.01456 m. An element with only the dipole coefficient, `k_normal=[0]`, stays finite.

title: `Sol(ks=0)` returns NaN positions
summary: A `Sol` with zero strength, `ks=0`, as when a solenoid is switched off in a scan or knob, returns NaN `x` and `y`, because the map divides by α = `ks`/2. The zero-field limit is a drift, since sin(αL)/α → L for length L, and both `Sol(ks=1e-9)` and `Drift` give it. A proton entering a 0.7 m `Sol(ks=0)` at `x` = 13 mm, `px` = 0.021, `y` = −17 mm and `py` = 0.008 exits with NaN `x` and `y` instead of 27.70 mm and −11.40 mm; the momenta and longitudinal coordinates are correct.

title: `ExactCFbend` octupole and decapole kicks lose all precision at small curvature
summary: `ExactCFbend` evaluates its octupole and decapole kicks as differences of order-one terms in 1 + x/`rc` and then multiplies them by powers of the bend radius `rc`, so rounding dominates at small curvature: the error scales as ε·`rc`³·k₃ for the octupole and ε·`rc`⁴·k₄ for the decapole, with k₃ and k₄ their coefficients and ε the double-precision machine epsilon. In the straight limit at y = 0 the decapole kick rate is −k₄x⁴/24, which a 60-digit evaluation of the code's own expression reproduces. For `rc` = 1000 m, `ds` = 1e-4 m, k₄ = 1e4 m⁻⁵ and a particle at x = 1 mm, the decapole changes `px` by −6.889e-6 instead of −4.167e-14.

title: Defocusing `ChrPlasmaLens` has the wrong arrival-time sign term
summary: In a defocusing `ChrPlasmaLens` (negative strength `k`), one arrival-time term proportional to (x² + y²)·`ds` keeps the sign of the focusing branch, so the arrival-time coordinate `t` is wrong and the map is not symplectic. Integrating the element's documented Hamiltonian (second order in the transverse variables, exact in `pt`) gives the correct `t`; the observed error equals the sign-flipped term to 2e-15 m. For a proton at γ = 2 with `ds` = 0.4 m, `k` = −2 m⁻², x = 0.01 m and y = −0.015 m, `t` is off by 1.459e-4 m with one slice and 1.713e-4 m with four, and the map's Jacobian M violates the symplectic condition MᵀJM = J by 0.01347. The transverse map and focusing lenses are correct.

title: Integer factorial overflow corrupts multipole normalization
summary: `Multipole` and `ExactMultipole` compute their factorial normalization in 32-bit integers, which overflow from 13! = 6227020800 on: thin `multipole=14` and above, and thick coefficients at index 13 and above. At y = 0 a normal multipole of integrated strength K and power n (n = `multipole` − 1 when thin) must change `px` by −K·xⁿ/n! with the exact factorial; one drift–kick–drift step of the thick element has the same exact expectation. On the CPU build, order-14 normal and skew kicks are 3.223 times too large (−0.003223 instead of −0.001 at x = 0.25 m), and order-18 kicks have the wrong sign and are 1.233e6 times too large. Orders up to 13 are correct; signed overflow makes higher-order values compiler-dependent.

title: `Buncher` uses the wrong transverse fields for spin transport
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), `Buncher` replaces the transverse RF fields with an effective magnetic field that reproduces the orbital kick but not the Thomas–BMT spin precession. Maxwell's near-axis fields of a localized axisymmetric RF field give a spin rotation about the vertical axis of −Ax/[2(γ + 1)] for a particle at offset x, with A = `k`·`V`, independent of the magnetic anomaly; a 65-digit quadrature confirms it. For a proton at γ = 2 in `Buncher(V=0.01, k=2)`, the spin rotation per metre of offset is +0.01529 rad/m instead of −0.003333 rad/m, wrong in sign and magnitude. The orbital kick is correct; the spin error persists for electrons, at γ = 10 and at low voltage.

title: Built-in H⁻ species has the wrong magnetic-anomaly sign
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), the built-in `Hminus` species uses the proton's magnetic anomaly a = 1.793 together with its negative charge, which reverses the ion's magnetic moment and its spin precession. Ground-state H⁻ has a closed electron shell and keeps the positive, slightly shielded proton moment; since the moment is (1 + a)qS/m for charge q, mass m and spin S, the negative charge requires 1 + a < 0, giving a ≈ −3.796. In a 0.1 T longitudinal field over 0.1 m at γ = 2, the built-in species precesses by +0.005146 rad instead of the Thomas–BMT value −0.005152 rad. Mass and charge are not affected, and an explicitly supplied anomaly gives the correct precession.

title: Weak nonzero `ChrAcc` acceleration corrupts transport and reference time
summary: `ChrAcc` with a tiny nonzero acceleration `ez` = qE/(mc²) (E the longitudinal electric field) divides a logarithm of a near-unity ratio and differences of nearly equal momenta by `ez`, so rounding corrupts the transverse map, the arrival time `t` and the reference time. A 65-digit quadrature of the documented Hamiltonian gives the correct values. For a proton at γ = 2 entering a 0.4 m element with `ez` = 1e-14 m⁻¹ at x = 0.01 m, `px` = 0.02, `x` exits at 0.01846 m instead of 0.01782 m, `t` is off by 0.002584 m and the reference `ct` is 0.4663 m instead of 0.4619 m. At `ez` = 1e-16 m⁻¹ the particle is not moved. Both signs fail.

title: Weak `ExactSbend` bends lose precision through cancellation
summary: `ExactSbend` with a very small nonzero bend angle `phi` loses precision, because its position update subtracts large bend-radius terms and nearly equal longitudinal momenta. A 65-digit calculation of the Lorentz trajectory to the exit plane gives the correct exit coordinates, which approach the exact drift as the angle goes to zero. For a proton at γ = 2 entering `ExactSbend(ds=0.4, phi=1e-12, B=0)` (`phi` in degrees) at x = 0.01 m with `px` = 0.02, `x` exits at 0.02190 m instead of 0.01782 m, an error of 4.075 mm; at `phi` = 1e-10 degrees the error is 0.02487 mm. Bends of exactly zero and of 10° are correct, and both curvature signs fail.

title: Rolled `ThinDipole`, `Sbend` and `ExactSbend` omit vertical steering
summary: Setting `rotation`, a roll about the beam axis, on a `ThinDipole`, `Sbend` or `ExactSbend` produces no vertical steering. The manual describes `rotation` as a rotation error, and the Lorentz force in a bend of angle θ rolled by α then gives a vertical kick `py` = −θ·sin α to leading order in θ; ImpactX gives `py` = 0. A 3 mrad bend rolled by 20 mrad misses a kick of −6.000e-5 (60 μrad), about 60 μm after a 1 m drift, so roll-error studies lose the leading vertical effect of rolled dipoles. Examples and the MAD-X importer also use `rotation` as a design roll, under which the reference orbit must bend vertically; under either reading the orbit stays in the horizontal plane.

title: `SoftSolenoid` omits transverse fringe-field spin precession
summary: With spin tracking enabled (experimental in ImpactX), `SoftSolenoid` omits the spin precession caused by the radial fringe field of a varying longitudinal field, because its spin map discards the field derivative. Maxwell's equations give the off-axis transverse fields −x·b′/2 and −y·b′/2 for b the longitudinal field divided by the rigidity Bρ; an independent Thomas–BMT integration with these fields disagrees with ImpactX while the orbits agree, and at vanishing magnetic anomaly ImpactX's spin does not follow the velocity, as it must. For a proton at γ = 3.3 offset by 20 μm in an asymmetric 0.7 m field profile, the transverse spin error at the exit is 1.548e-4. On-axis precession is correct.

title: Low-energy `ExactDrift` corrupts co-moving arrival times
summary: At low energy, `ExactDrift` shifts the arrival time `t` of particles moving at the reference energy and direction, because its longitudinal-momentum radical subtracts the separately rounded terms (1/β − `pt`)² and 1/(βγ)², with β and γ those of the reference. Such particles must keep their relative arrival times, as a 90-digit evaluation of the drift confirms. For a proton (rest energy 938.27208816 MeV) at 1 keV kinetic energy, a 1 m drift adds 0.002379 m (7.9 ps) to `t`, shifting the bunch centroid; off-energy and inclined particles get timing errors up to 0.002454 m and transverse errors up to 1.013e-7 m. At 1000 MeV the errors stay below 1e-16 m; at low energy their sign and size depend on floating-point rounding.

title: `ExactCFbend` reverses the skew-decapole horizontal kick
summary: `ExactCFbend` applies the skew-decapole (`k_skew[4]`) horizontal kick with the wrong sign: it is the negative of the derivative of the documented vector potential (Zolkin 2017, Table XI), while the vertical kick is correct. The map is therefore not symplectic, and an independent integration of the curvilinear Hamiltonian reproduces ImpactX to 1.3e-14 only with the sign reversed. For a proton at γ = 3.25 in a 0.15 m bend with curvature 2 m⁻¹ and skew strength 160 m⁻⁵, a particle at x = 0.08 m, y = −0.05 m exits with `px` off by 1.321e-4, and the Jacobian M violates MᵀJM = J by 6.795e-4. Spin tracking (experimental) uses the same wrong field, with spin errors up to 7.899e-4.

title: `CFbend` spin coupling is singular at coincident frequencies
summary: With spin tracking (experimental), `CFbend` divides its spin coupling by k + (Gγh)², for gradient k, magnetic anomaly G and curvature h = 1/`rc`, which vanishes when the vertical focusing frequency √(−k) equals |Gγh|. The Thomas–BMT solution stays finite there; on the design orbit it is a rotation by GγhL about the vertical axis over length L. For electrons at γ = 0.5/G = 431.2 in a `CFbend` with `rc` = 1 m, `k` = −0.25 m⁻² and L = 0.31 m, all spin components are NaN while the orbit is correct. Nearby the spins are finite but wrong: at γ = 2 with G = 0.25 and the gradient detuned by a relative 1e-15, the error is 7.450e-5.

title: Eigenemittance diagnostics corrupt small or repeated modes
summary: With eigenemittance diagnostics enabled, `beam_moments()` returns wrong eigenemittances, or three NaNs, when the beam's emittances differ widely or two are equal, for both particle beams and `Envelope`. In the source, the characteristic cubic is formed from differences of trace invariants, which loses the small modes, and `acos` is then evaluated without guarding its domain. For an uncoupled beam the documented eigenemittances equal the projected normalized rms emittances, which an independent Hermitian eigensolver reproduces to within 5×10⁻¹⁵ relative. At γ = 2, an uncoupled beam with normalized emittances 0.01, 0.02 and 1000 µm gives eigenemittances 0.05116, 0.05584 and 1000 µm, and 1, 1 and 1000 µm give three NaNs. A moderate spread (1, 2 and 3 µm) is correct, as are the projected emittances.

title: Nonlinear `DipEdge` optics omit `K5` fringe focusing
summary: For a `DipEdge` with the nonlinear fringe model, the linear transfer matrix that ImpactX reports, which envelope tracking uses, omits the vertical focusing from the fringe-field integral `K5`, which the particle map includes. The reported matrix must equal the particle map's small-amplitude derivative, whose vertical focusing changes in proportion to g·`K5`·sin ψ/cos³ψ (ψ the pole-face angle, g the gap). For a proton of 1000 MeV kinetic energy with ψ = 0.2 rad, `rc` = 1 m, g = 0.1 m and `K1` = 0, raising `K5` from 0 to 0.1 changes the particle map's R₄₃ = ∂py/∂y by 0.002110 m⁻¹, matching an independent derivation from its generating function, while the reported matrix is unchanged.

title: Phase-space legends label geometric emittance as normalized
summary: The phase-space plot from `plot_phasespace()` labels its legends with the normalized-emittance symbols εₙ,x, εₙ,y and εₙ,t but displays the geometric emittances. ImpactX documents the normalized emittances as the diagnostic keys with an `n` suffix, equal to β₀γ₀ times the geometric values, with β₀ the reference speed over c and γ₀ the reference Lorentz factor. For a proton beam at γ₀ = 7, the x legend shows 168.7 nm while the normalized emittance is 1168 nm, a factor β₀γ₀ = 6.928. The numerical diagnostics are correct; only the plot annotation is wrong, by the factor β₀γ₀.

title: PIC `2p5D` longitudinal kick uses a fixed 1 m reference length `r0`, which `Gauss2p5D` exposes
summary: With `2p5D` particle-in-cell space charge, the longitudinal kick multiplies the absolute 2D potential, whose logarithmic kernel implicitly fixes a reference length r₀ = 1 m that `2p5D` cannot change. Scaling all lengths at fixed charge and energy must leave the length-scaled kick unchanged; for a 1 pC electron bunch at γ = 10 the transverse kick obeys this, while the longitudinal kick changes by 7.879% when lengths double. Against the exact 3D field of a long round Gaussian bunch with γσz/σ⊥ = 50 (σz, σ⊥ the rms length and width), the on-axis longitudinal field has L2 errors of 73.62% (σ⊥ = 1 mm), 131.1% (σ⊥ = 0.1 mm) and 149.9% in a round pipe of radius 25 mm.

confirmed.scope: physics review of the reference length

title: ISR uses the electron classical radius for every species
summary: With incoherent synchrotron radiation (ISR) enabled, ImpactX uses the electron classical radius for every species, although the radiated power scales with the species radius r_q = q²/(4πε₀mc²). Classical radiation theory gives the ultrarelativistic fractional momentum loss over a path ds at bending radius ρ as (2/3)·r_q·(βγ)³·ds/ρ². A 7 TeV (kinetic) proton reference over 100 m at ρ = 2800 m loses 9.954×10⁻⁹ of its momentum instead of 5.421×10⁻¹², 1836 times too much. Electrons are correct, but ISR accepts any species, and an ion of mass M and charge Ze radiates M/(Z²mₑ) times too much; from the source, the same radius also sets the quantum-excitation variance.

title: `wakeconvolution.w_t_rf` has the wrong functional form
summary: The Python helper `impactx.wakeconvolution.w_t_rf`, the short-range dipole wake W⊥(s) of a periodic accelerating structure at distance s behind the source, uses the bracket u·e⁻ᵘ with u = √(s/s₀) (s₀ a fitted length), where the cited Bane model (SLAC-PUB-9663, 2003, Eqs. 15–16) has 1 − (1 + u)·e⁻ᵘ. Bane's form rises linearly in s at short range; the implemented one starts as √s. For a cell resembling the Next Linear Collider design (iris radius 4.92 mm, gap 6.89 mm, period 8.75 mm) the wake is 19.34 times too large at s/s₀ = 0.01 and 1.392 times at s/s₀ = 1. Its documentation also calls it a resistive-wall wake and states units of V/m/pC/mm although it returns SI. Built-in tracking does not call it.

title: `Gauss2p5D` underweights the initial quadrature interval
summary: `Gauss2p5D` space charge computes its transverse forces with a quadrature that treats the initial interval [0, δ], δ = `gauss_taylor_delta`, separately, and divides that interval's contribution by three a second time when it completes the Simpson sum. The forces therefore carry a bias that does not vanish as the number of quadrature points grows. Direct integration of the Gaussian Coulomb convolution, checked against Gauss's law for a round beam, gives the correct forces. With δ = 0.01, 4001 points and a test particle at (x, y) = (σx, 0.6σy), aspect ratio σy/σx = 0.25 gives relative errors of −5.736×10⁻⁵ in px and −1.648×10⁻⁵ in py; aspect ratio 4 gives −2.312×10⁻⁴ and −8.103×10⁻⁴. At the default 101 points, ordinary Simpson discretization error adds to this bias.

title: The 3D PIC beta interface loses the supplied Lorentz factor
summary: For 3D FFT particle-in-cell space charge, ImpactX passes only the rounded velocity β = √(1 − 1/γ²) to the WarpX/ABLASTR Poisson solver, which reconstructs the Lorentz factor γ from it, while ImpactX's own coordinate transforms keep the original γ. Lorentz similarity requires the transverse kick scaled by (βγ)² to stay unchanged for a fixed rest-frame source and mesh. At γ = 6.000×10⁷ (30.66 TeV electrons) the solver uses γ = 4.745×10⁷, and for a uniform sphere on a 64³ mesh the rescaled transverse kick is 9.642% low, on a normalized kick of only 1.735×10⁻²⁰. The error shrinks at lower energy, to 2.716×10⁻⁹ at γ = 10⁴.

title: A tracer can erase weighted beam size and emittance
summary: `beam_moments()` can report zero beam size and emittance for a finite-emittance beam when a distant particle with zero or tiny weight, such as a tracer, is stored first. The moments are accumulated about the first stored particle, so the shifted second moment and squared mean nearly cancel and the core variance is lost. Weighted standard deviations and emittances must not depend on particle order or zero-weight particles; a two-pass weighted covariance gives the correct values. For a core with σx = 10⁻⁹ m and emittance εx = 10⁻¹² m and a tracer at x = 1 m stored first, with weight 0 or 10⁻²⁴, both are reported as 0; stored last, they are correct.

title: Phase-space charge histograms ignore particle weights
summary: The phase-space plot from `plot_phasespace()` labels its charge histograms Q [C/bin] but counts macroparticles instead of summing their charges q_ref·w, where q_ref is the reference-particle charge and w the number of real particles a macroparticle represents. The displayed values are therefore counts, and bins whose particles carry different weights also have wrong relative charges. For a 1.550 nC test beam, a 2×2 x–px histogram shows 16 in every bin instead of the charges from 8.613×10⁻¹¹ to 8.613×10⁻¹⁰ C that a direct sum of q_ref·w gives, and splitting each macroparticle into two half-weight copies doubles every bin while the beam is unchanged. The numerical charge and moment diagnostics are correct.

title: Longitudinal plot scale and units disagree by 1000
summary: The phase-space plot from `plot_phasespace()` multiplies the longitudinal momentum pt, the energy deviation −ΔE/(P₀c) with P₀ the reference momentum, by 1000, the factor it uses to convert transverse momenta to mrad, while the axis label states units of p₀c with no scale factor. ImpactX documents pt as dimensionless, so a per-mille display must state its factor. A beam with pt = ±0.004 is plotted at ±4. Tracking and stored coordinates are unaffected; values read from the plot are 1000 times too large.

title: `Thermal` negative-charge initialization returns NaN positions
summary: Initializing a `Thermal` distribution for a negatively charged species, such as electrons or H⁻, with positive focusing strength k and nonzero bunch charge returns NaN for every particle position, while the momenta are finite and the call returns normally. In the source, the radius calculation raises a self-field coefficient formed with the signed species charge to the power 2/3. Reversing the charge sign leaves the repulsive self-force unchanged, so the distribution must equal that of the opposite charge; an independent integration of Gauss's law with a Boltzmann density gives that finite solution. In the electron and H⁻ cases all 2049 positions are NaN, while positive species give finite positions and, at zero bunch charge, both signs give identical results.

title: MAD-X `PC` leaves the reference energy at its default
summary: When a MAD-X lattice's `BEAM` command gives the momentum `PC` instead of `ENERGY`, importing it into ImpactX (for example with `RefPart.load_file()`) leaves the reference total energy at the parser's 1 GeV default; `GAMMA`, `BETA` and `BRHO` are ignored the same way. MAD-X derives the total energy E from any of these, for `PC` as E = √((pc)² + (mc²)²), and native MAD-X does so for the same input. A proton `BEAM, PC=2` (2 GeV/c) starts at 61.73 MeV kinetic energy instead of 1271 MeV, so the reference velocity and rigidity are wrong too. Lattices that give `ENERGY` import correctly; the only warning printed is the importer's general preview notice, which does not mention `PC`.

title: MAD-X ion import discards explicit mass and charge
summary: Importing a MAD-X `BEAM, PARTICLE=ION` with explicit `MASS` and `CHARGE` into ImpactX discards both in favor of a fixed default ion mass and charge, so the reference mass, charge, kinetic energy and rigidity are wrong before tracking starts. MAD-X documents independent mass and charge overrides for ions, and native MAD-X keeps them for this input. For an alpha particle, `BEAM, PARTICLE=ION, MASS=3.7273794, CHARGE=2, ENERGY=10` (GeV), ImpactX uses a mass of 939.6 MeV and charge 1, giving 9060 MeV kinetic energy instead of 6273 MeV. The importer prints that it ignores `MASS` and `CHARGE`; an unrecognized particle name keeps them.

title: Marker insertion multiplies an exact bend's angle
summary: `insert_element_every_ds()`, which places a thin element such as a `Marker` at regular spacing by splitting the thick elements it falls in, gives each piece of a split `ExactSbend` the full original angle `phi`. A uniform sector bend of length L and angle θ must keep its total deflection when split, so a piece of length Lᵢ needs the angle θ·Lᵢ/L; the analytic exit coordinates of that arc fix the correct result. A marker at the midpoint of a 1 m, 20° `ExactSbend` makes it bend by 40° in total, and markers every 0.3 m make 80°, while the path length stays 1 m. This holds with `B=0` or an explicit field; `Sbend`, `CFbend`, `Quad` and `ChrAcc` split exactly.

title: `before_slice` length changes retain stale collective-kick lengths
summary: If a `before_slice` hook changes the length `ds` of the upcoming element, ImpactX transports the element over the new length but applies its space-charge kick for the length cached before the hook. The hook contract allows modifying the upcoming element, the same change made in `before_element` gives the correct result, and independently composed drift and kick matrices reproduce both outcomes. For a 10 MeV, 0.1 A proton envelope with 1 mm rms sizes and 2D space charge, retuning a drift from 0.1 to 0.2 m halves the kick: the normalized-momentum variance ⟨pₓ²⟩ ends at 1.270×10⁻⁸ instead of 2.058×10⁻⁸ with Strang splitting. Retuning from 0.4 m doubles the kick and from zero length omits it, in first-order and Strang splitting; particle tracking shares this code.

title: Survey reverses normalized-quadrupole focusing for negative charge
summary: `plot_survey()` draws each quadrupole above or below the axis according to the sign of `k`·charge, but `Quad.k` and `ChrQuad(unit=0).k` are already normalized by the signed rigidity, so a positive `k` focuses horizontally for either charge. The plot's docstring defines a positive height as horizontal focusing, and particle tracking and the analytic transfer matrix confirm the focusing direction for both charges. A 0.5 m `Quad` with `k` = 1 m⁻² focuses a 1000 MeV electron exactly as it does a proton (matrix element R₂₁ = −0.4794 m⁻¹), yet it is drawn with height −0.8 instead of +0.8. For electrons and other negative species every `Quad` and normalized `ChrQuad` is drawn reversed; tracking is correct, and `ChrQuad` with a physical gradient (`unit=1`) is drawn correctly.

title: PALS import discards quadrupole tilt and skew
summary: Importing a PALS (Particle Accelerator Lattice Standard) lattice into ImpactX ignores a quadrupole's tilt `tilt1` and skew coefficient `Ks1`: the converter builds a normal quadrupole from `Kn1` (or `Bn1`) alone and warns about neither. PALS defines the normalized coefficient as (`Kn1` + i·`Ks1`)·exp(−2i·`tilt1`); an independent matrix calculation from it and native rotated `ChrQuad` elements agree on the correct transport. For a γ = 5 proton at x = 1 mm in a 0.2 m quadrupole with k = 2 m⁻², a 90° tilt gives the normalized momentum pₓ = −3.947×10⁻⁴ instead of +4.054×10⁻⁴, and `Kn1=0, Ks1=2` gives p_y = 0 instead of 4.000×10⁻⁴. Untilted normal quadrupoles import correctly; a skew quadrupole without `Kn1` is rejected with an error.

title: PALS import discards body offsets and active apertures
summary: Importing a PALS (Particle Accelerator Lattice Standard) lattice into ImpactX silently ignores body offsets (`BodyShiftP`) and apertures (`ApertureP`) on drifts and quadrupoles. A body shift d displaces the element and its field, so a particle u is transported as M·(u − d) + d for element map M; native `ChrQuad(dx=d)` and `Drift` plus `Aperture` give them. For a γ = 5 proton, a 0.2 m quadrupole with `Kn1` = 2 m⁻² offset by 1 mm leaves an on-axis particle at normalized momentum pₓ = 0 instead of 3.947×10⁻⁴, and a 0.2 m drift with an active ±1 mm rectangular exit aperture passes all four particles where two should be lost. An inactive aperture correctly has no effect.

title: Dashboard imports the bundled proton cyclotron with electron mass and charge
summary: The ImpactX dashboard's import of Python input files ignores `set_species()` and keeps its electron mass and charge defaults, so the bundled `cyclotron/run_cyclotron.py` example, which sets a proton reference, imports as an electron. Importing a script must preserve the species it defines; replacing `set_species("proton")` with explicit mass and charge setters does preserve it. At the example's 4 keV kinetic energy K the imported magnetic rigidity is −2.137×10⁻⁴ T·m instead of +9.139×10⁻³ T·m, the proton value of Bρ = √(K(K + 2mc²))/(qc).

title: Dashboard Twiss import corrupts scientific notation and drops negative alpha
summary: The ImpactX dashboard's import of Python input files reads Twiss parameters with a pattern that keeps only the mantissa of numbers in scientific notation and skips negative values. Re-importing the dashboard's own export must restore the same beam, whose covariance follows from the Courant–Snyder parameters β, α and the emittance ε. A Gaussian beam exported with `beta_x=1`, `emitt_x=1e-6` and `alpha_x=-0.5` re-imports with `emitt_x=1` and no `alpha_x`, so the initial x variance is 1 m² instead of 1.000×10⁻⁶ m². The omitted `alpha_x` keeps the interface's previous value; at the default of zero this also removes the 5.000×10⁻⁷ m x–pₓ correlation. The y and t emittances lose their exponents as well; an emittance written in fixed-decimal form imports correctly.

title: Dashboard envelope commands omit the selected beam intensity
summary: In envelope tracking mode, the ImpactX dashboard generates `sim.init_envelope(ref, distr)` without the selected beam intensity, so the envelope starts with zero bunch charge and its space-charge kicks vanish. `init_envelope` defines the intensity as bunch charge in C for 3D space charge and current in A for 2D, and the bundled envelope example passes it. Running the generated code for a 10 MeV proton envelope with 1 nC selected, through a 0.2 m drift with 3D space charge, leaves the normalized-momentum variance ⟨pₓ²⟩ at its vacuum value 1.000×10⁻⁸ instead of 3.889×10⁻⁵, the result of a closed-form uniform-ellipsoid field calculation. ImpactX logs a zero-charge warning; according to the source, the dashboard's Run and Export both use this generator.

title: Dashboard silently accepts a partial lattice when repeated cells are unresolved
summary: When the ImpactX dashboard imports a Python input file whose lattice includes a repeated cell, such as `sim.lattice.extend(cell * 3)`, it drops the repetition without a message and accepts the preceding elements as the complete lattice. The ImpactX manual documents this form, and an importer that cannot evaluate it must report an incomplete import. A 0.4 m drift followed by three cells of a 0.2 m drift and a 0.1 m quadrupole (k = 2 m⁻²), 1.3 m in total, imports as the single 0.4 m drift, so for a 10 MeV proton the transfer-matrix focusing term R₂₁ is 0 instead of the analytic −0.5510 m⁻¹. The same lattice written out element by element imports all seven elements, and a single unrepeated cell imports correctly.

title: Dashboard reimports envelope and reference exports as particle tracking
summary: A simulation exported from the ImpactX dashboard in envelope or reference tracking mode re-imports as particle tracking: the export writes only the tracking call (`track_envelope()` or `track_reference(ref)`), and the import does not read it and keeps its particle-tracking default. The import is meant to restore the configuration the file describes, and that call identifies the tracking model directly. An envelope export, `sim.init_envelope(ref, distr)` followed by `sim.track_envelope()`, regenerates as `sim.add_particles(bunch_charge_C, distr, npart)` and `sim.track_particles()`, and the two bundled envelope examples the dashboard offers also import as particle tracking. The changed mode is visible in the interface; particle-mode exports and scripts with an explicit `tracking_mode` assignment keep their mode.

title: MAD-X `BV=-1` retains forward straight-multipole polarity
summary: When ImpactX imports a MAD-X lattice for a reversed beam (`BV=-1`), straight normal and skew multipole strengths keep their forward-beam polarity, because the importer omits the `bv` factor. MAD-X defines `BV=-1` as reversing the magnetic force, native MAD-X applies it, and the importer's own documentation specifies the reversal; analytic maps and an independent integration of the equations of motion give the reversed result. For a 1.4 GeV (total energy) proton in a 0.23 m quadrupole with `k1` = 1.7 m⁻² and tilt 0.21 rad, a test particle exits with normalized momentum pₓ = −7.699×10⁻⁵ instead of +2.189×10⁻⁵. The reversed polarity applies to body quadrupoles, sextupoles and octupoles and to thin quadrupole through dodecapole terms; forward beams and kickers import correctly.

title: Harmonic-only MAD-X ring cavities import at zero frequency
summary: Importing into ImpactX a MAD-X ring whose `RFCAVITY` gives only the harmonic number h (`HARMON`), without `FREQ` or a beam `FREQ0`, creates a `ShortRF` with zero frequency and prints a warning. MAD-X derives the frequency from the ring circumference C as f = hβc/C, and native MAD-X does so for the same decks: a 1.4 GeV (total energy) proton ring with C = 73 m and h = 17 needs 51.82 MHz. For a 0.73 MV cavity at zero crossing, the slope of the energy kick along the bunch is 0 instead of −7.630×10⁻⁴ m⁻¹, so the cavity gives no longitudinal focusing. Cavities with an explicit `FREQ` or `FREQ0` import correctly; a source comment requires `HARMON` and `FREQ0` together, but the importer's documentation does not.

title: Programmable reference callbacks lose mutations without a retained live wrapper
summary: A `Programmable` element's reference-particle callback loses its changes to the reference particle unless the script holds a Python object for `sim.beam.ref` while tracking. The documented contract applies the reference update before beam transport with no such prerequisite, and analytic drift and energy-gain formulas give the required result. A 0.375 m programmable drift traversed over three periods at γ = 1.25 leaves the reference at s = 0 instead of 1.125 m, and an electron energy update leaves γ at 1.050 instead of 1.250, after which the beam's normalized momenta are off by up to 1.376×10⁻⁴. Holding `sim.beam.ref` gives the correct result, as the bundled example and tests do; holding only `sim.beam` or a copy of the reference does not.

title: Dashboard variable refresh leaves equal elements at stale lengths
summary: In the ImpactX dashboard, when several equal elements, such as identical drifts, have their lengths bound to one lattice variable, changing the variable can leave some at the old length, because the update finds elements by value equality instead of identity. N drifts bound to a length L must total N·L. For eight equal drifts bound in reverse order and changed from 0.125 m to 0.375 m, the exported lattice is 2.5 m long instead of 3 m, and a test particle at γ = 3.5 exits at x = −1.600 mm instead of −1.700 mm, with no error shown. Binding in index order or giving the drifts distinct names avoids it.

title: CSR-only dashboard exports omit required particle shape
summary: A simulation set up in the ImpactX dashboard with coherent synchrotron radiation (CSR) enabled and space charge disabled is exported without the required `particle_shape` setting, so the generated script raises `RuntimeError` ("particle_shape is not set") in `init_grids()`. The generator tests `if not state.space_charge`, but disabled space charge is the string `"false"`, which is truthy, so the shape line is skipped. ImpactX requires a particle shape whenever CSR is enabled; for 24 electrons at 75 MeV through a 0.125 m drift, inserting `sim.particle_shape = 1` before `init_grids()` lets the export run to s = 0.125 m. Exports with CSR off, or with CSR and 3D space charge, set the shape and run.

title: Marker insertion compresses field profiles and repeats linear maps in each piece
summary: `insert_element_every_ds()`, which places a thin element such as a `Marker` at regular spacing, splits the thick elements it falls in by copying them with a shorter `ds`, so each piece of a split `RFCavity`, `SoftQuadrupole` or `SoftSolenoid` holds a compressed copy of the whole field profile. A midpoint marker in a 1 m cavity with profile ½(1 − cos 2πs/L) cuts a 10 GeV electron's energy gain by 20.00%, to 0.1735 MeV instead of 0.2169 MeV; the unsplit cavity and ImpactX's own `nslice=2` subdivision match the analytic gain integral. Constant profiles are unaffected. It also splits `LinearMap` and `SpinMap`, documented as unsliceable, without an error, and each piece applies the whole map: a 60° `SpinMap` rotation becomes 120°.
